description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20).  Fixture ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/review/s492a/circ/CircA.pm + CircB.pm (two modules that `use` each other, each with the BEGIN block above -- the spelling that makes a circular import WORK in perl, because @EXPORT is set before the other module's `use` runs) + r1998a.pl: perl prints `a:B b:a:B`; PCL on main 33513766 AND on the s492a tree: `read error during load: Package Exporter does not exist.  Line: 49, Column: 54` in the module's emitted file (e.r1998a.tree beside it).  So it is not #1998's bug and not caused by its fix; the four quadrants s492a probed all set @EXPORT at file level.
SUSPECT (measure first: print line 49 of the emitted module text): the BEGIN block's body is emitted with a package-QUALIFIED symbol `|Exporter|::...` that the CL READER meets before anything has created the package -- `in-package`/package existence is a READ-time fact per top-level form (memory: reference_in_package_is_read_time), and the `require Exporter` that would create it is INSIDE the same form.  Discriminate: the same two lines at FILE level (the everyday spelling -- must already work, thousands of modules do it), then inside BEGIN without the circular `use`, then with `use Exporter "import";` instead.  Fix shape follows from which of the three fails: most likely the compile-phase block must ensure the packages it names exist (a `p-defpackage`/ensure form hoisted ahead of the BEGIN form) -- the mechanism `use` already relies on.
Guard: the CircA/CircB fixture as a Pl/t module-loading row beside s492a's circular-use-01.t.
subject: LOAD CRASH (pre-existing; found by the s492a review probe): a module that sets up Exporter inside a BEGIN block -- `BEGIN { require Exporter; our @ISA = ("Exporter"); our @EXPORT = ("a_fn"); }` -- dies at load with a CL READ ERROR "Package Exporter does not exist"
